senses.gloss:
A-rājānaḥ, ‘not princes,’ is a term used to describe persons in two passages of the Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, and in the aitareya brāhmaṇa. Weber also finds them mentioned in the Atharvaveda, and thinks that they--Sūtas (‘charioteers’) and Grāmaṇīs (‘troop-leaders’) there referred to--were called thus because, while not themselves princes, they assisted in the consecration of princes.
